stages.title: First programs
stages.summary: By the end you can write a program that asks questions and uses the answers.

stages.title: Decisions
stages.summary: By the end your programs react differently to different answers.

stages.title: Loops
stages.summary: By the end you can write games that keep going until someone wins.

stages.title: Functions
stages.summary: By the end your programs are built from small named parts.

stages.title: Lists and text
stages.summary: By the end you can hold and work with many things at once.

stages.title: Dictionaries and data
stages.summary: By the end you can model real information: records, counts and lookups.

stages.title: Files and errors
stages.summary: By the end your programs remember things between runs and survive bad input.

stages.title: Classes and bigger programs
stages.summary: By the end you can organise a program across several files.

stages.title: Python in the real world
stages.summary: By the end you can write the kind of script that does a real job.

stages.title: Git and GitHub
stages.summary: By the end your work has a history you can rewind, and you can read and publish projects.

stages.title: Other people's code
stages.summary: By the end you can read, fix and extend code you have never seen, and build a real project from nothing.
